status: FINAL — reviewed and accepted 2026-10-09. v2 INCONCLUSIVE verdict preserved.
reason: v2 returned INCONCLUSIVE on the strict sampling-uniformity check (|dt-0.0005| < 1e-6 s). Investigation of the timing mechanism shows the v2 threshold conflated permitted timing variation with numerical comparison strictness. This amendment derives the sampling rule from the verified output-timing mechanism.

decimal_arithmetic.method: Python decimal module (28-digit precision) on raw CSV timestamp strings; measurement window [0.6, 2.6] s, 4001 samples.
decimal_arithmetic.finding: Maximum |dt - 0.0005| is EXACTLY 0.000001 s (1 us). 2330 intervals deviate by exactly 1 us; 0 intervals exceed 1 us.
decimal_arithmetic.correction: The earlier reported 1.0000000004169e-06 s was floating-point representation noise. The boundary equality itself (exactly 1 us) fails the strict < 1e-6 s rule. The 4e-16 s excess does not explain the failure; the failure is at the boundary.

timing_mechanism.verified_behavior: TH output is written at the first solver step with simulation time TT >= the scheduled mark. The timestamp written is the actual step time TT (which overshoots the mark), not the mark itself. The next output is scheduled at mark + /TFILE (schedule remains anchored to marks).
timing_mechanism.consequence: Each output time t_k = mark_k + u_k, where u_k in [0, dt_solver) is the overshoot. Inter-output intervals satisfy |dt_k - 0.0005| = |u_{k+1} - u_k| < dt_solver.
timing_mechanism.distinguishing_test: All 4001 overshoots (t_i - i*0.0005) are >= 0 (never negative), consistent with 'first step past mark'. Maximum written overshoot 1.1 us. Timestamp strings carry 7 significant digits; a 1-us overshoot exceeds the 0.05-us rounding quantum, confirming genuine step-time overshoot, not CSV quantization of exact marks.
timing_mechanism.solver_dt: Engine log reports DT=1.0602E-06 s (element-stable, constant). The overshoot bound is therefore dt_solver = 1.0602 us.

one_us_bound_assessment.question: Is an inclusive <= 1 us bound justified?
one_us_bound_assessment.answer: No. The verified mechanism permits overshoot up to dt_solver_max = 1.0602 us, which exceeds 1 us. Observed written overshoot reaches 1.1 us.
one_us_bound_assessment.conservative_bound_derivation: Let true output time = mark + e_i, e_i in [0, dt_solver_max). Then dt_i - dt_scheduled = e_{i+1} - e_i, so |dt_i - dt_scheduled| < dt_solver_max. Written timestamps add rounding rho_i with |rho_i| <= r_i. Conservative written-interval bound: |dt_i - dt_scheduled| <= dt_solver_max + r_i + r_{i+1} = 1.0602 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 2.0602 us (using the larger rounding above 1 s to cover the full window).
one_us_bound_assessment.justified_bound: |dt - 0.0005| <= 2.0602e-6 s. The earlier draft value of 1.2e-6 s is withdrawn; it used the sub-1-s rounding quantum across the whole window.

estimator_validation_extension.method: Mechanism-faithful validation (validate_interp_v4.py): true times t_k = k*0.0005 + u_k with u_k ~ Uniform[0, 1.0602e-6) s; written timestamps rounded to 7 significant digits (%.6e); signal synthesized at true times; estimator derives f_s from written timestamps and assumes uniform spacing (as the protocol does). Same 1440-case grid (3 quantities x 480).
estimator_validation_extension.finding: Maximum observed errors: logmag 0.001838 Hz, magnitude 0.001934 Hz, power 0.002029 Hz (480 cases each).
estimator_validation_extension.scope_note: Observed maximum over the tested conditions (mechanism-faithful jitter plus timestamp formatting). Not a general accuracy bound for all possible signals.

timestamp_format.method: Empirical inspection of all 5400 CSV timestamp strings; converter source in separate repo (OpenRadioss/Tools), not inspected.
timestamp_format.finding: All timestamps match %.6e (7 significant digits). Format confirmed empirically, not from source.

rounding_by_magnitude.0.6_to_1_s: decimal spacing 0.1 us; max rounding error 0.05 us per timestamp
rounding_by_magnitude.1_to_2.6_s: decimal spacing 1 us; max rounding error 0.5 us per timestamp

timestamp_format.correction: An earlier draft used a constant 0.05 us rounding uncertainty across the window. This was wrong: above 1 s the spacing is 1 us, so per-timestamp rounding reaches 0.5 us and the combined interval uncertainty reaches 1.0 us.

solver_dt.finding: DT is 1.0601e-6 or 1.0602e-6 s throughout; dt_solver_max = 1.0602e-6 s.

revised_sampling_rule.exact_clause: Inter-sample intervals in the measurement window must satisfy |dt - 0.0005| <= 2.0602e-6 s, where dt is computed from the output timestamps. The bound is derived from the verified TH output-timing mechanism (hist2.F: output at first solver step with TT >= mark; |e_{i+1} - e_i| < dt_solver_max = 1.0602e-6 s per engine log) plus timestamp representation rounding (%.6e format confirmed empirically on all 5400 timestamps; r = 0.5 us per timestamp at/above 1 s, conservative for the full window): 1.0602 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 2.0602 us.
revised_sampling_rule.replaces: v2 adequacy_checks.checks.sampling_uniformity.criterion (|dt - 0.0005| < 1e-6 s) and amendment-1 detail_3_sampling to the extent it references the v2 uniformity threshold.

comparison_tolerance.exact_clause: Numerical comparisons against the 2.0602e-6 s bound use inclusive <= with timestamps compared as exact decimals (or floating-point with epsilon 1e-12 s). The comparison tolerance (numerical) is separate from the permitted timing variation (physical, 2.0602e-6 s). A deviation of exactly 2.0602e-6 s passes; a deviation exceeding 2.0602e-6 s by more than the numerical epsilon fails.
comparison_tolerance.note: This separates the two concepts v2 conflated: how much timing variation the mechanism permits vs how strictly we compare numbers.

estimator_validation_scope.exact_clause: The estimator accuracy validation is extended to the mechanism-faithful timestamp conditions: true output times t_k = k*0.0005 + u_k with u_k ~ Uniform[0, 1.0602e-6) s, written timestamps rounded to 7 significant digits (%.6e format), signal synthesized at true times, estimator deriving f_s from written timestamps (validate_interp_v4.py). The maximum observed error from the extended sweep (logmag: 0.001838 Hz over 480 cases) applies to these tested conditions. The v2 bound (0.00184 Hz maximum observed error) remains valid only for the uniform-sampling conditions actually tested in v2.
estimator_validation_scope.replaces: v2 estimator.validation conclusion language to the extent it implies the bound covers non-uniform sampling.

preserved.v2_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE (2026-10-09 run) stands unchanged under v2+amendment-1. This amendment does not retroactively alter it.
preserved.diagnostic_findings: f1 = 40.3768 Hz (0.962% below 40.7690 Hz reference); release checks A and B PASS (J_A = -2.00046 N-s, J_B = 0.00108 N-s); all other adequacy checks PASS. Preserved as diagnostic findings alongside the terminal v2 verdict.
preserved.reanalysis_label: Any v3 analysis of the 2026-10-09 artifacts is REANALYSIS of previously observed data, not a new measurement. It must cite this amendment and the revised rule before execution.
